note:
THE FIRST ROUND NOT DRIVEN BY A CRITIC. The player played the game and gave six notes; they replaced REFERENCE_BAR.md and every verdict in rounds/verdicts/ as the bar. Three of his six described damage this project's own measurement loop had caused, and every one of those had scored as an improvement at the time.

WHAT SHIPPED
* SLOW-MO DELETED (his note 3). score.js had emitted it on every cut, 0.16-0.34x for 0.30-0.85 s, built as a combo reward. Removing it also repaired the measurement layer: the beat labelled '+250 ms' was really 91.7 ms and '+1000 ms' was 716.7 ms. Every beat is now exact. So when the round-3 critic compared juice at '+250 ms' against plate-01 and cut every lifetime 3-4x, it was looking at a frame nearly three times earlier than it believed.
* JUICE: IT WAS A VELOCITY BUG, NOT A LIFETIME BUG (his note 1). A rim bead's median asymptotic travel was 2.20 units against a 6.93-unit half-width — it could not reach the frame edge at ANY lifetime. Drag constants were 9-62 where physically faithful drag for 1.7-14 mm droplets at this world's gravity is 1-4. Share of each class getting off-screen before dying: rim 4.8%, spray 7.0%, mist 0.0%. Now 96% / 74-80% / 56-64%. `life` is no longer authored at all — it is solved per droplet from its own ballistic exit.
* PHYSICS: RAPIER RIGID BODIES (his note 2). Interpenetration median 1.276 -> 0.008 units on five converging fruit and 1.065 -> 0.000 on four melon halves, measured by separating-axis over 48 directions on the world-space render meshes — a metric that cannot invent an overlap. His convex hull question answered with a number: 0.98-1.4 ms per cut in-browser, and only because the cloud is reduced from 10,908 loose vertices to <=48 exact support points first. Naive would have been a 34 ms hitch per melon, on precisely the input he says drops frames.
* STAGE: specular and DOF pulled back (his notes 5 and 6), staged as three separate captures so each change is attributable.
* PERF: 33 draw calls / 88.7k triangles landscape, 53 / 96.9k portrait, against 120 / 250k. Draw calls FELL while a physics solver was added, because contacts shove fragments out of the visible box sooner and round 10's budget governor retires them earlier.

THE BEST DIAGNOSTIC OF THE ROUND IS A CONTROL NOBODY ASKED FOR. His note 4 gave two symptoms, 'jank low poly' and 'spiky'. The shape bake-off includes column T: the shipped geometry with 72% MORE TRIANGLES and nothing else changed. It is indistinguishable from the shipped column, and a watermelon limb is 0.16 px from a perfect circle at either tier. THE POLYGON COUNT WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM. The spikes were, and the spikes are ours — the orange's five horns are the r9/r10 navel, the apple's lumpy twist is r10's lobe, the kiwi at r10's strongest setting reads as a gnarled peanut. Three rounds of critics demanded outline events and got them. The fix is cheap: variant D is 1.20x triangles against B's 1.71x, because removing spikes removes mesh. AWAITING HIS CHOICE — he asked to pick before anyone commits a round to it.

TWO MORE INSTRUMENT FAILURES FOUND
(1) THE PERF PROBE HAS BEEN MEASURING A SCENE TWICE AS HEAVY AS REAL PLAY. The complexity probe spawns and cuts on a TICK schedule while the world runs on the SIM clock, so slow-mo doubled the population it measured. Rounds 4-10 checked the ceilings against a fiction. Realistic-play population is unchanged (mean bodies 5.8 -> 5.7).
(2) THE R1b FAST-VS-SLOW PAIR WAS NEVER CONTROLLED: 15-fast-flick and 16-slow-cleave were sampled at 25.0 and 16.7 ms of sim time after settles of 141.7 and 75.0 ms. The two beats that exist to bracket blade speed differed by the harness, not by the game.

AND ONE CROSS-FILE CANCELLATION, CAUGHT THE RIGHT WAY. Deleting slow-mo made ctx.timeScale identically 1, which turned stage.js's `fdt = dt * (0.35 + 0.65*timeScale)` into plain `dt` and decayed the blade flare 1.75x faster — silently undoing round 10's bleach. The feel owner does not own stage.js: it measured the damage in a file it was not allowed to touch and published the coefficients rather than letting a critic find it. Recalibrated by the derived 0.571x; core_sat lands at 0.112, inside the acceptance band, not back at r10's 0.017. A further 30% coefficient change moved it 0.008, so the flare decay is no longer the dominant lever and the residual is left for a critic rather than tuned by eye on a confounded baseline.

OPEN: the velocity-dependent spray/blob mix (his latest note, spec'd as the Weber number in rounds/reports/r11-PLAYER-NOTE-juice-mix.md); harness hardening (reject unknown flags, refuse zero-luma frames, seed the loop, explicit window for clip on 08-citrus-caps); framedrop on split (cutGeometry allocates per half on the main thread); portrait's REFERENCE_BAR framing auto-fail; and the 3.94 MB bundle from Rapier's inlined WASM.

pieces.name: Game feel & timing
pieces.biggestGap: Slow-mo removed; the combo reward is now visual rather than temporal. Cadence measured and deliberately NOT retuned — the probe evidence disagreed with itself in sign and it needs a human thumb.
pieces.fix: Player to confirm the game does not now feel rushed.

pieces.name: Juice fluid
pieces.biggestGap: Droplets now exit frame ballistically instead of fading in place; drag was 3-20x too high across every layer.
pieces.fix: The velocity-dependent spray/blob mix (Weber number) is spec'd and NOT yet implemented.

pieces.name: Rigid bodies (NEW)
pieces.biggestGap: Interpenetration effectively gone; restitution 0.30 chosen by eye from a sweep (0.05 reads as dead clay, 0.60 as billiards).
pieces.fix: Bundle is 3.94 MB from inlined WASM; splitting it out is open.

pieces.name: Lighting, grade & DOF
pieces.biggestGap: Specular and DOF pulled back per the player. Flare decay recalibrated after slow-mo's removal silently changed it.
pieces.fix: core_sat residual 0.112 vs r10's 0.017, on a confounded baseline — for a critic.

pieces.name: Fruit silhouette
pieces.biggestGap: THE POLYGON COUNT WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM — a 72%-more-triangle control is indistinguishable from the shipped mesh. The spikes are ours, from three rounds of critics demanding outline events.
pieces.fix: AWAITING THE PLAYER'S COLUMN CHOICE from rounds/reports/r11-shape-bakeoff.png.
